The game looks nice for an indie. Sounds and visuals are good. Enemies are relatively interesting compared to other titles. But. 1. There are a lot of bugs. Menus don't work, buttons don't click and such. 2. Weapons and upgrades are weak and boring, and, again, very very weak. I'm not saying this because it was hard (the difficulty is ok, I beat the first level on my 2nd try). I'm saing that after 8 level-ups of the same weapon, it started shooting 6 bullets instad of 4, and the damage was a bit higher. So after putting everything in one weapon, it becomes maybe twice stronger as its default version. What is this?.. The upgrades (skills) are also horrible. 10% movespeed? 0.5m pickup radius? This is just nothing, they don't make a noticable difference unless you max them out, and even after that they are very very meh. The usual balance is also not there. There are clear outliers that are better at level one than some other weapons when maxed out. 3. The flow during the mission wasn't thought through either. You are constantly bombarded with events that lead you in opposite directions. Event and main mission spawns are also completely random - once I had a mission from the start of the level where I had to walk for 10 minutes straight to reach the destination (while also being bombarded by events that I couldn't complete because I had to keep moving towards the mission). 4. Extremely weird design decisions like some abilities, if they kill enemies, prevent them from dropping loot. WTF? Overal, I understand the feeling of a) wanting to make a somewhat difficult game b) wanting to be different from other VSs But those choices are just... bad.

I did only 2 runs so far and won both, one where I finished on timer and one where I managed to kill the boss at the end before timer run out, can't say I would recommend this game right now for these reasons: - Weapons feels bad to use no matter how much you upgrade them - they are not weak since I clearly managed to "beat the game" in 2 tries, but they feel weak, boring and uninteresting, I don't know if its the vfx/sfx or the upgrades but all the starter weapons you can get your hands on during the first few runs are missing that oomph that makes them satisfying to use - Maybe add way more enemies and go crazy with the weapon upgrades? - I do like that the game actively give you random objectives so you have something to do, but all the objectives spawn somewhere far away from you so you have to actively walk there to do it - at least this is the case for the ones that I managed to do - For a 1.0 release but with only 2 characters to use one of which you have to unlock is not great (I unlocked the second character on my 2nd run) Beside these points I think this is an okay game for the price tag, great arts, I enjoyed the enemies designs and the challenge of trying to kill the boss before timer, I hope it will get more updates to improve the game even more especially the weapons Edit: - After giving it more try (at the third map now), I feel even worse, the weapons are boring and feel bad to use, the only cool weapon I like so far is a cluster rocket that transform into a nuke after 4 attacks but for some reason is way slower than the normal attack, which delay your next attack a lot even with all the cooldowns buffs you have, so you have to sit there and wait for the nuke to explode - which i feel like dont even do that much more damage than a normal attack - to end before your next attack can happen, and since you have to put every upgrades you can into that one weapon, good luck surviving the last few minutes when enemies are swarming you and you gotta beg the nuke to explode faster so your next rocket cluster can go off. - Devs please I think you need to reconsider the game speed, everything is so slow and boring even near the end of a run with all the upgrades, some weapons just perform way better than others, please make the current upgrades feel fun to use.

The game is a decent "survivors" clone that has unique visual style and varied and fitting music selection. However its game mechanics, level design and progression systems are very generic. It also feels light on content. I'm not recommending it because at this point you need more to stand apart in a crowded genre. There is nothing "wrong" with the game tho and it is quite cheap, so if you like the genre and want to scratch that bullet hell itch, go for it, just don't expect anything new.

Its fun, it has quality, its just not ready yet. What i played was overall a good game, but 1.) it didnt set itself off all the other games in the genre with anything. Its literally as if they tried to copy Vampire Survivors the first weeks it came out, not coming late to the party years later. For that its just not doing anything unique. Theres so many possibilities to do something special with the concept and yet it stays so basic. 2.) The content isnt there yet too. Its 3 characters, about a dozen weapons and the most basic passives. Thats it. Your meta progression is not providing enough for long and also felt a bit too shallow, at least too short. Whats left? Visual quality and sounds are great. Beyond that theres not much to say. It does the basic formula good, but im not seeing where this goes to provide something unique and fun. The title implies you might be defending an area or base, maybe be on a battlefield with NPCs fighting the hordes and you do your job. This could have actually been a unique concept that followed the thought of their first game. In fact, what they do here is what i missed in their first game. If they now fused both together, they had something going on. Yet the game never really pulled off the "Onslaught" or the "Let them come". Because the entire premise is that you were somehow flying around, got hit by alien arm and now try to survive until a bomb goes off. And again, this could have been a cool idea if the gameplay and premise followed through. If you look for the most basic VS clone, go for it. Its fine, just not special. As of now i hope the devs have an idea that will turn this into a special game with its own unique twist.

I do enjoy the retro visuals. There is a more robust meta-progression system; however, that system is marred by power-ups that feel anything but powerful or even useful. There is a good assortment of weapons from which to choose, sadly half to most most of them outright suck even with their prototype variants. Stats and stat bonuses/power-ups you get don't feel impactful. If I have 100%+ Cooldown Reduction on something, I should be seeing it roaringly fire off instead of going from a mild saunter to a brisk walk. At higher difficulties, the bonuses to damage may not even be there. There is a cool hidden system that some passive bonus upgrades will give you an extra perk upgrade to a different or same passive stat; however, there s no way to increase these chances. Not even going to talk about how the different characters don't even really matter. And the hit detection (towards the enemies AND players) is god awful. In an over-saturated genre, this game is "meh" at best. It is a frustratingly bland addition. At $8? You could probably buy two games in the game-play vein of this one and still have more fun out of each of them individually, than you would here. If it's on sale? Cool. If not, I'd pass. Hard.

*Please take hours played into consideration. Your experience may vary (please don't yell at me)* 99/140 71% Visual Clarity 5/10 Appropriate Speed 10/10 Difficulty 10/10 Control 4/10 Grind 10/10 Risk vs Reward 2/10 Enemy Attack Variance 7/10 Battlefield weapon upgrades 8/10 Reason to explore the map 8/10 Run variance 3/10 Difficulty transitions 8/10 Meta Upgrades 7/10 Endless Mode 7/10 Accessibility 10/10 Highlight- Starting at hard difficulty, the game excels at making you feel the panic of being closed in on by the horde. With limited dodge/utility you will feel the pinch more than once in a good way. Biggest Drawback-Endless locked and relegated to hardest difficulty keeping you from the mindless god mode endgame state that we all love. Visual Clarity-Enemies are easy to see even with explosions but some obstacles may become obscured leading to death. Not adjustable. Appropriate Speed-Characters move well relative to enemy speed and speed power ups are desirable but not overpowered. Difficulty -Each stage of difficulty (normal/hard/endless) are noticeable and some preparation is required before moving on. Jumping from normal directly to endless has appropriate consequences. Control-Weapons upgrades are set with the evolution being between 2 possibilities but not player selectable. Banishes and rerolls are very limited. There is also a small selection of weapons essentially choice comes down to which to upgrade first and which 3-4 weapons to pass on each run(due to limited rerolls). Some shrines offer powerful temporary power ups with the option to pick from 3. Grind-Following each stage and difficulty unlocks will allow the player to unlock most things are they are needed without repetition. Risk vs Reward-Only present by which weapons to take and whether to take an objective or abandon the effort. No upgrades/choices have drawbacks nor gambles. Enemy Attack Variance-Enemies have projectiles both slow and fast moving, the damnable exploding enemies, Bosses have their own attack patterns. Points deducted due to hitbox unpredictability. Battlefield weapon upgrades-Each weapon gets substantial upgrades and each evolution changes how the weapon behaves greatly with only a few exceptions. Extends into endless. Reason to explore the map-The map contains dynamic enemy and player damaging obstacles, strong power ups/shrines, location bases power ups, and meta upgrades scatter throughout. Missions appear at regular intervals requiring travel. Marked down slightly due to the small variety of shrines. Run variance-3 characters and 4 stages and 18 weapons would put it in the midrange, but it is severely hampered by the set upgrades of the weapons. Difficulty transitions-The game does very well with the progression to the next difficulty. Marked down slightly for gating endless to be the hardest difficulty rather than for each difficulty. Meta Upgrades-Meta Upgrades are varied and some have more impact that just numbers though nothing too crazy. Everything's general, nothing character or weapon specific Endless Mode-The most difficult mode. Offers continuing upgrades some not number bases (flame thrower gets more jets etc.). Many more missions are given in the mode to keep you busy. Marked down due to loss of access to the mode at lower difficulties requiring substantial time to unlock and even more to not die immediately. Accessibility -Full controller support! While heavily music focused, all relevant actions (missions, boss moves, powerups etc) can be enjoyed without sound. Additionally, colorblind options are available. Awesome; no complaints here only praise. Note for one handed controller play that dodge and utility actions are present but not fully necessary to use (keyboard remains active during controller use :) ).

A great game worthy of its modest price tag, a Vampire Survivors clone that gets the damage scale correct and makes you want to return to play it again and again. On top of all this, the developers are fantastic. I posted a bug with their latest update, and they pushed a patch within the hour. That’s worthy of praise. So I am going to complain about it for the rest of this review. It’s so frustrating when games get this close to perfection. The hit detection on one’s character is not accurate; let’s get that out of the way. Second, and more importantly, the initial meta-upgrades are useful. Literally 90% of the rest are so situational, you can invest thousands of credits for something that may never activate during a run. I mean, you got the Vampire Survivors formula so well done and forget that the meta-upgrades are literally the draw for the game. And like literally every game in this genre, the playable characters are horrifically unbalanced, with one character clearly more powerful than all the others. Add to that the game’s insane difficulty curve. I have bought every upgrade. I can purchase the three consumable buffs. Normal and Hard difficulties are cakewalks. Onslaught is damn near impossible. Seriously, did these developers actually play this game? And the newly added endless mode is barely as long as a traditional run, so what’s the point? One of the staples of the Vampire Survivors model is that it is designed for people without twitch reflexes. It’s for people who want to chill with a game. If you are not a fifteen-year-old, you should be able to grind a game to completion. Well, after 17 hours, with a difficulty spike stopping my enjoyment, I’m incline to walk away as there is no reason to keep playing. I got no more upgrades, and the game has gotten too hard. Not really the route for positive reviews. But yeah, 17 hours for less than $10, it’s fun, play it.

Received as a gift from a friend. Technically, a vast improvement over Let Them Come. The growth of the devs themselves is probably the most impressive thing here. The genre shift is an odd but not unwelcomed choice, and Onslaught itself is a decent little bullet heaven, if a bit barebones. You'll run out of content after roughly 7-10hrs, which isn't too big a deal given the price, but I can understand why some people find it lacking. If there are any major cons, it's that the devs chose to play it safe and there are no real shake-ups that set it apart from its peers. I will give some kudos for that transition screen, though. If you grab it, do so during a sale.
